response:
To counter Tate & Liza's Psychic-types without using Sharpedo or Absol, catch a Corphish to evolve into Crawdaunt or a Duskull to evolve into Dusclops, and level your team past 40 [1][2][3][4][5].

### Top picks

**Corphish** (Psychic-Immune Attacker)
Catch on Route 102 with the Super Rod (Lv20-45) before Tate & Liza [1]. Corphish evolves into Crawdaunt at level 30, becoming a Water/Dark-type [2]. This gives it complete immunity to the Gym's Psychic attacks, while its Water typing hits Claydol, Lunatone, and Solrock for super-effective damage [3].
**Backup:** Sableye. Found in Granite Cave (B2F) by walking (Lv10-12) [6]. Its Dark/Ghost typing grants immunity to Psychic attacks and gives it zero elemental weaknesses in Generation III [7].

**Duskull** (Bulky Ghost Attacker)
Catch at the Mt. Pyre summit by walking (Lv26-30) before Tate & Liza [4]. Duskull evolves into Dusclops at level 37, a Ghost-type with excellent defensive stats to withstand Tate & Liza's attacks [5][3]. It can deal super-effective damage to their entire team, and its Levitate ability makes it immune to Claydol's Earthquake [8].
**Backup:** Spheal. Found in Shoal Cave (B1F) by walking (Lv26-32) [9]. A bulky Water/Ice type that evolves into Sealeo at level 32, providing super-effective Water damage against three of the Gym's Pokémon [10].

### Battle Notes
*   **Tate & Liza:** They use Claydol (Lv41), Xatu (Lv41), Lunatone (Lv42), and Solrock (Lv42) [8][11][12][13]. 
*   All carry Psychic, which deals 2x damage to Breloom [14]. 
*   Solrock's Sunny Day + Solar Beam combo is a 4x threat to Marshtomp/Swampert, Claydol's Earthquake is super-effective on Manectric, and Claydol's Ancient Power threatens Swellow [14]. 
*   You should level your team to around 42 [8]. Marshtomp evolves into Swampert at 36, and Manectric learns Bite (a Special Dark move in Gen III) at 39 [15][16].

***

**Assumptions**
* The player will level up their team to at least level 40-42 before fighting Tate & Liza, allowing their newly caught Pokémon to evolve.

**To sharpen this**
* Do you have the TM30 Shadow Ball from Mt. Pyre to teach to your Ghost-type attacker?

What didn't work about the last picks—are they too tedious to catch, do you dislike the designs, or do they take too long to level up?

citations.label: Bulbapedia: Walkthrough:Pokémon Emerald/Part 14 § Mossdeep City > Mossdeep Gym

plan.headline: To counter Tate & Liza's Psychic-types without using Sharpedo or Absol, catch a Corphish to evolve into Crawdaunt or a Duskull to evolve into Dusclops, and level your team past 40.

recommendations.why: Corphish evolves into Crawdaunt at level 30, becoming a Water/Dark-type. This gives it complete immunity to the Gym's Psychic attacks, while its Water typing hits Claydol, Lunatone, and Solrock for super-effective damage.

alternatives.why: Its Dark/Ghost typing grants immunity to Psychic attacks and gives it zero elemental weaknesses in Generation III.

recommendations.why: Duskull evolves into Dusclops at level 37, a Ghost-type with excellent defensive stats to withstand Tate & Liza's attacks. It can deal super-effective damage to their entire team, and its Levitate ability makes it immune to Claydol's Earthquake.

alternatives.why: A bulky Water/Ice type that evolves into Sealeo at level 32, providing super-effective Water damage against three of the Gym's Pokémon.

battle_notes.note: Tate & Liza use Claydol (Lv41), Xatu (Lv41), Lunatone (Lv42), and Solrock (Lv42). All carry Psychic, which deals 2x damage to Breloom. Solrock's Sunny Day + Solar Beam combo is a 4x threat to Marshtomp/Swampert, and Claydol's Earthquake is super-effective on Manectric. Claydol's Ancient Power also threatens Swellow. You should level your team to around 42. Marshtomp evolves into Swampert at 36, and Manectric learns Bite (a Special Dark move in Gen III) at 39.

assumptions: The player will level up their team to at least level 40-42 before fighting Tate & Liza, allowing their newly caught Pokémon to evolve.
follow_up_questions: Do you have the TM30 Shadow Ball from Mt. Pyre to teach to your Ghost-type attacker?
